G-DPA_2.headline: Record how your processors may engage sub-processors
G-DPA_2.teaser: For each processor: authorised one by one, or in general.
G-DPA_2.fromNis2: Your NIS 2 contract clauses on subcontracting are a start. The GDPR also asks how you authorise each sub-processor: one by one, or in general with notice of every change and a chance to object (Art. 28(2)).
missed: Under a general authorisation the processor informs you of any intended addition or replacement of a sub-processor, so that you can object (Art. 28(2)). Make sure these notices reach someone who reads them.
The processor must impose on every sub-processor the same data protection obligations it has towards you (Art. 28(4)).

learn.title: Who works for your provider
body: Many processors engage further processors themselves, known as sub-processors, for example a software provider its data centre. It may do so only with your prior written authorisation (Art. 28(2)).

The authorisation comes in two forms: specific, for each sub-processor one by one, or general. Under a general one the processor informs you of every intended change, and you can object. The authorisation is often in the data processing agreement, with a list of sub-processors.
learn.duty: The GDPR requires a processor to engage further processors only with your company's prior specific or general written authorisation.

examples.title: What a sound clause looks like
examples.caption: Two agreements, read against Art. 28(2)

good.value: Our cloud provider may engage sub-processors under a general authorisation. It lists them online, announces every new one a month ahead, and we may object.
good.note: A general written authorisation with notice of every intended change and a chance to object, as Art. 28(2) asks. Keep the announcements.

bad.value: Our payroll provider may use any subcontractor it likes. We are not told who.
bad.note: Without a prior authorisation, and without notice of changes under a general one, the clause falls short of Art. 28(2). Ask the provider for its sub-processor list and the clause.

authorisation.title: How you authorised
authorisation.lead: For each processor: what does the agreement say about sub-processors? Look it up there, usually under "sub-processors" or "subprocessing".

done.title: Your authorisations are recorded
done.note: Under a general authorisation, read your providers' change notices and object when a new sub-processor does not suit you.
